record.original_question: Must homotopic closed geodesics in a manifold of dimension ≥ 3 with no conjugate points be homotopic through closed geodesics?

evidence.quote: Must homotopic closed geodesics in a manifold of dimension ≥ 3 with no conjugate points be homotopic through closed geodesics?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $M$ be a smooth complete Riemannian manifold of dimension at least $3$ with no conjugate points (i.e., for every geodesic $\gamma:\mathbb{R}\to M$ and every pair of distinct parameters $s\neq t$, no nonzero Jacobi field along $\gamma$ vanishes at both $s$ and $t$). Let $\gamma_0,\gamma_1:S^1\to M$ be two closed geodesics that are freely homotopic, i.e., there exists a continuous map $H:S^1\times[0,1]\to M$ with $H(\cdot,0)=\gamma_0$ and $H(\cdot,1)=\gamma_1$. Must there exist such a homotopy $H$ with the additional property that for every $s\in[0,1]$ the loop $H(\cdot,s):S^1\to M$ is itself a closed geodesic of $M$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in published open problem lists about geodesics on manifolds without conjugate points. While it is known that freely homotopic closed geodesics in such manifolds have equal length, no source found in the search resolves whether they must be connected by a path of closed geodesics in dimension ≥ 3. No definitive solution was located.

status_evidence.title: Open problems and questions about geodesics (Burns–Matveev)
status_evidence.snippet: Compiled list of open problems on geodesics including questions on manifolds without conjugate points.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed among open questions about geodesics on manifolds without conjugate points.

status_evidence.title: Closed geodesics on surfaces without conjugate points
status_evidence.snippet: Studies counting and structure of closed geodesics in free homotopy classes on surfaces without conjugate points.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses closed geodesics in free homotopy classes for the no-conjugate-points setting but in dimension 2.
